chapter.title: Package management
chapter.para: DHS does not prescribe a package format. Any package manager that installs into a DHS system MUST keep the guarantees of this chapter.

section.title: The base is never overwritten
section.para: A userland package MUST NOT place a file at a path the base already provides. Such files are left out of the installation. This keeps the base intact under the overlay and makes the userland removable.

section.title: Receipts
section.para: For every installed package the package manager MUST record a receipt in /overlayer/zexlib/registry that lists each file it installed. Removing the package MUST delete exactly those files.

section.title: Libraries
section.para: Before installing a package, the package manager SHOULD check that every shared library its programs need is provided by the system or by a package being installed with it, and ask the user before installing otherwise.

listitem.para: New base packages are downloaded and verified while the system runs, and staged in /overlayer/.syshub-pending. The staging directory is writable only by the package manager running as root and is protected against change while it waits.
At the next boot the initramfs applies the staged upgrade to /overlayer/syshub before the system view is composed ().
The previous state SHOULD be kept so that the last upgrade can be rolled back from the boot menu or the kernel command line.

section.title: Protected paths
section.para: The base and boot layers SHOULD be protected against accidental change even by the administrator: the privilege tool SHOULD refuse destructive commands (removing, moving, overwriting, shredding) on /overlayer/syshub, /overlayer/zaisys, /overlayer/.syshub-pending and /overlayer itself. The base changes only through base upgrades.

note.title: Implementation note
note.para: Zainium OS replaces sudo with elevate, which refuses rm, rmdir, mv, cp, rsync, shred and unlink on those paths.
